s1.where: The starting screen where I would type a new question
s1.expectation: I think this is the opening screen of the app, where you begin a new conversation. I am guessing, because nothing actually says so.
s1.cue: Only the words 'Ask ChatGPT' in the typing box at the bottom, and the three suggestions 'Start a voice chat', 'Create an image or sticker', 'Write or edit'. There is no title at the top; the top row has a menu button, a 'Get Plus' button and a round icon I cannot read.

first_pass.why: The screen is calm and uncluttered, which I appreciate, but it has no name. The top of the screen, where I look first, holds an advertisement for 'Get Plus' instead of a title. I have to work out where I am from a placeholder in a text box, and a placeholder is not a name. If I came here after getting lost, I could not confirm I was at the start.
first_pass.solution: Put a plain title at the top, such as 'New chat', in large text where 'Get Plus' sits now.

test_cases.action: Open the app on your phone (if something else is showing, press the round-arrow home/back only as described below). Before tapping anything, say where you are and what told you. Then tap the three-line button at the top left, tap 'Library', come back with the arrow at the top left, and — if the side panel is showing — tap the dimmed area on the right to close it. Say again where you are.
test_cases.real_if: it is real if, both times, nothing on the page lets you name where you are
test_cases.not_real_if: it is not real if something on the page lets you name it
test_cases.what_happened: I opened the app and it came up on the first page, with the keyboard already open over the bottom half. Before touching anything I looked for a name: the top row was the three-line button, 'Get Plus', and a round icon. The only words were 'Ask ChatGPT' in the typing box and the two suggestions 'Create an image or sticker' and 'Write or edit'. I would call it 'the start page' only because I remember it. I opened the side panel, tapped 'Library' (that page does say 'Library' at the top), tapped the arrow, which opened the side panel again, and tapped the dimmed area to close it. I was back on exactly the same page, and again nothing on it gave me a name. Both times, nothing named where I was.

s1.closing_comment: On the phone the first page still has no name, and with the keyboard open there is even less on it. I know it is the start only because I remember it.

s2.where: A message box about the microphone, over a chat screen
s2.expectation: I am being told to turn on the microphone in the phone's settings before I can use Voice. Underneath, I think I am still on a chat screen, but I am guessing about that part.
s2.cue: The message box: 'Please enable microphone access in System Settings to use Voice' with 'Cancel' and 'Open settings'. The greyed-out 'Ask ChatGPT' box at the bottom.

first_pass.why: The message itself is well written and I understand what it wants. But it has no title, and the screen behind it has no name either, so I know what is being asked of me, not where I am. The line 'You will be redirected to Android settings' also warns me I am about to be taken somewhere else, which is the kind of move that loses me.
first_pass.solution: Give the message a short heading like 'Microphone needed for Voice', and name the screen behind it, so that when I press Cancel I know what I am returning to.

test_cases.action: (Not run: the entry that opened that box is no longer on the app's first page, and reaching it another way would mean starting voice, which is not allowed.)
test_cases.reason_not_run: The tester said it could not be run: the entry that opened the microphone box is no longer on the first page, and reaching it another way would mean starting voice, which is not allowed.

s2.closing_comment: I could not test it, so my view from the picture stands as it was.

s3.where: A gallery of picture ideas, with the 'Trending' tab chosen
s3.expectation: I think I am in a part of the app for making pictures, looking at a 'Trending' list. I am guessing at the name of the section; I can only see the name of the tab.
s3.cue: The tab row with 'Trending' shaded and 'Templates' beside it, the labels on the pictures like 'Sketch' and ''80s flashback', and 'Create image' in the box at the bottom.

first_pass.why: The shaded 'Trending' tab does tell me which list I am on, and I can see it is chosen. But 'Trending' names a list, not a place. There is no title saying this is the pictures section. And the screen is dominated by large photographs and drawn faces, which I cannot use to orient myself; they cost me effort without telling me anything about where I am.
first_pass.solution: A title at the top, such as 'Images', above the Trending and Templates tabs, and fewer, smaller pictures above the fold.

test_cases.action: Tap the three-line button at the top left, then 'Images'. Before scrolling, say where you are and what told you. Then scroll the pictures down a little, stop, and — without scrolling back — say where you are now.
test_cases.real_if: it is real if, after the small scroll, nothing on screen lets you name the page
test_cases.not_real_if: it is not real if you can still name it from what you see
test_cases.what_happened: I opened the side panel and tapped 'Images'. The page came up with the notice 'Your generated images moved to Library' printed across the top, over the back arrow, just as in the pictures. Below it were the 'Trending' and 'Templates' tabs, with 'Trending' shaded. There was no title naming the page; I could only say 'the Trending list, somewhere for pictures', and I knew it was 'Images' only because I had just tapped that word. Then I scrolled down a little and stopped. The tabs and the notice scrolled away completely. What remained was the back arrow floating over a grid of photographs and faces: 'Sketch', 'Stickers', ''80s flashback', 'Oktoberfest throwback'. Nothing on the screen let me name the page at all. When I scrolled back up, the notice had changed shape and now sat below the arrow as a card with its own X.

s3.closing_comment: Even the 'Trending' tabs, the only thing I could hold on to, scroll away after a small scroll. Then there is nothing on the page but faces and photographs.

s4.where: The start screen with the 'Write or edit' options open
s4.expectation: I am on the start screen and I have picked 'Write or edit'; it now offers me writing choices. I am fairly sure.
s4.cue: The bold heading 'Write or edit' above the choices 'Improve flow', 'Rewrite for clarity', 'Turn ideas into an outline', with a close cross beside it. The typing box now says 'Write anything'.

first_pass.why: The heading is large, bold and says exactly what I chose, and the three options below all match it. The cross next to it tells me how to leave. I would prefer it at the top of the screen rather than near the bottom, where I have to look for it, but once found it is unambiguous.

s5.where: The page for buying the ChatGPT Plus plan
s5.expectation: I am on the page describing and selling the 'ChatGPT Plus' subscription. I am sure.
s5.cue: The very large heading 'ChatGPT Plus', the feature list with 'Free' and 'Plus' columns, and the button 'Upgrade for $19.99'.

first_pass.why: The heading is big and at the top, and everything below it agrees with it. I know where I am. One thing I did have to stop on: in the 'Go' and 'Plus' switch, the grey half is 'Plus', and grey usually means switched off to me. Only the heading told me that grey meant chosen.

s6.where: The page for buying the ChatGPT Go plan
s6.expectation: I am on the page describing the 'ChatGPT Go' plan. I am sure.
s6.cue: The large heading 'ChatGPT Go', the 'Free' and 'Go' columns, and 'Upgrade for $8.00'.

first_pass.why: The heading names the page clearly and matches the price button. As on the previous page, the chosen half of the switch, 'Go', is the grey one, which I would otherwise read as not chosen; the heading settles it for me.

s7.where: A temporary chat that will not be saved
s7.expectation: I am in a 'Temporary chat', a conversation that will not be kept in my history. I am sure.
s7.cue: The heading 'Temporary chat' in the middle, the line 'This chat won't appear in history', and 'Temporary chat' again in the typing box.

first_pass.why: The name is large and is repeated in the typing box, so I get it twice. The explanation under it is plain. It sits in the middle of the screen rather than at the top, but on an otherwise empty screen my eye goes straight to it.

s8.where: The settings panel for a temporary chat
s8.expectation: I have opened the settings for the temporary chat and am choosing between 'Personalized' and 'Unpersonalized'. I am sure.
s8.cue: The bold panel heading 'Temporary chat settings', the two choices with explanations, and the 'Done' button. 'Temporary chat' is still visible, faded, behind it.

first_pass.why: The panel has its own clear heading, and I can still see the screen I came from behind it, so I know both where I am and where 'Done' will return me. Each option is explained in a full sentence.

s9.expectation: I have opened the main menu of the app, which lists its sections and my past conversations. I am fairly sure it is the menu, but I cannot tell which section I came from.
s9.cue: The panel sliding in from the left with the heading 'ChatGPT' and the list 'Images', 'Library', 'Projects', 'Scheduled', 'Plugins', then a list of conversations and 'See all...'.

first_pass.why: 'ChatGPT' is the name of the app, not of this menu, so the heading only tells me which app I am in. None of the menu entries is marked as the one I am currently in, so the menu cannot tell me where I was. Below the sections, there is a long list of conversation titles with no heading separating them from the sections, which blends two different kinds of thing together.
first_pass.solution: Mark the section I am currently in, and put a heading such as 'Recent chats' above the list of conversations so it is clearly separate from the sections above.

test_cases.action: From the app's first page tap the three-line button at the top left. Say which part of the app you are in right now. Tap 'Library'; then tap the arrow at the top left to come back — the side panel opens again. Look at it: does anything on it show you where you just were? Then tap a conversation name in the list below the line, and open the side panel again: does anything show where you are now? Close it by tapping the dimmed area on the right.
test_cases.real_if: it is real if nothing on the side panel ever marks where you are
test_cases.not_real_if: it is not real if the side panel marks where you are or were
test_cases.what_happened: From the first page I opened the side panel. The heading said 'ChatGPT', and none of the sections ('Images', 'Library', 'Projects', 'Scheduled', 'Plugins') was marked, nor was any conversation; I could only say 'the menu'. I tapped 'Library' and then the arrow: the side panel opened again, and 'Library' was not marked, so the panel did not show me where I had just been. Then I tapped the conversation 'Adjust writing tone' below the line, and later opened the panel again. This time 'Adjust writing tone' had a grey band across it. So the panel does mark the conversation I am in. Later I went to 'Images' and came back with the arrow, and the panel still shaded 'Adjust writing tone', not 'Images'. So it marks the conversation I will return to, but it never marks a section like 'Library' or 'Images'. The list still has 'Create red apple image' and 'Create Red Apple Image' one above the other, and 'Greeting exchange' twice, with nothing to tell them apart.

s9.closing_comment: The side panel does mark the conversation I am in with a grey band, which I did not expect. But it never marks a section like 'Library' or 'Images', and the identical conversation names are still there.

test_cases.action: Tap the three-line button, then 'Images', then the flower picture at the top left ('Sketch'). Say where you are. Swipe up once across the big white area. Say where you are now, and whether you are still on the same screen. Then tap the X at the top left of the panel and choose 'Discard' (that only throws away your own lines).
test_cases.real_if: it is real if you cannot say where you are on the panel, or if the swipe takes you somewhere else
test_cases.not_real_if: it is not real if you can name where you are before and after the swipe
test_cases.what_happened: From 'Images' I tapped the flower picture labelled 'Sketch'. A white panel slid up over the bottom of the page, with an X, a pencil, a shapes symbol, an eraser, an undo arrow, a slider and a row of colours. It had no title; the word 'Sketch' was on the picture I had tapped but not on the panel. I could only say 'a drawing panel over the pictures page'. I swiped up once across the white area. It did not move me anywhere: the pencil drew a black line, and I was plainly still on the same panel, with the 'Trending' tabs still visible above it. When I tapped the X, a small box asked 'Discard sketch?' with 'Keep editing' and 'Discard'. That was the first time I saw the word 'sketch' anywhere on the panel. I chose 'Discard' and was back on the pictures page. So the swipe did not throw me to a different screen as the pair of pictures t32 suggested, but the panel itself still never named itself until I tried to leave.

s10.closing_comment: The drawing panel still has no name while I am on it. The word 'sketch' only appears when I try to leave.
